I'm thinking through the row-oriented algorithm's dependency structure: each row's off-diagonal entries depend on prior rows' diagonals, which are finalized before being used, while the diagonal for the current row is computed in-place.\n\nTo preserve bit-identical results matching the hash output, I need to maintain the exact sequential summation order per element rather than reordering floating-point operations. Since element (i,j) depends on earlier entries in row i and column entries up to j in row j, I can parallelize across independent elements while keeping each individual sum's order fixed—processing by column or wavefront seems like the right strategy for exposing parallelism without breaking the dependency chain.\n\nBit-identical results aren't guaranteed with FMA anyway, so I won't fuss over that. As for the matrix generation step, that's O(n^3) but untimed, so I'll keep it sequential on CPU and focus GPU effort purely on the decomposition kernel itself, since that's what's actually being benchmarked.\n\nFor timing, I'll include host-device transfers inside the decomposition function's timed region since that reflects the real cost of the operation on host data. For the non-positive-definite detection, syncing back to host per column to check each diagonal value would hurt performance with many columns, so I need a way to check the diagonal without a per-column round trip -- maybe flagging the failure on device and only syncing once at the end.\n\nOn performance, launching one kernel per column means n launches doing roughly O(j*n) work each, which is fine for moderate n but the overhead and memory-bound naive dot products become a real bottleneck at larger sizes due to poor coalescing across rows. I'm weighing a blocked right-looking approach against a simpler left-looking column-wise kernel where threads handle different rows for a fixed column, accepting some inefficiency for correctness and simplicity given the effort budget.\n\nActually bit-identity doesn't matter here anyway since accumulation order differs between right-looking and left-looking approaches regardless of implementation — the original presumably sums contributions sequentially while a blocked version sums in a different order, changing rounding. Since validation only checks relative error to 1e-6, this discrepancy is acceptable.\n\nI'm thinking through the failure-path behavior: if a column fails during factorization, I need to preserve the same early-exit semantics so A's partial contents on failure match what the original leaves behind, rather than continuing to launch all remaining column kernels regardless of the earlier failure.\n\nTo do this cheaply, I'm considering a device flag that records the first failing column index via an atomic min, with the host periodically checking it every 32 columns rather than syncing on every single one, balancing correctness against the overhead of repeated host-device synchronization.\n\nChecking every 64 columns avoids stalling the launch pipeline while keeping overhead low. Now I'm sketching the per-column kernel design, starting with the diagonal computation that sums contributions from prior columns.\n\nThe diagonal entry needs a sequential dot product of length j before the column update kernel runs — trivial cost even at n=4096, so I can keep it as a separate single-thread kernel launched just before the column kernel, accepting two launches per column since overhead is small and stream-ordered execution pipelines them well.\n\nFor the column kernel, I'm now thinking about memory layout: each thread handles a row i>j and computes a dot product against row j using shared memory tiles, but the stride-n access pattern for L[i*n+k] across threads in a warp is suboptimal. Storing L transposed (column-major, LT[k*n+i]) would make those warp reads contiguous across i instead, which is a much better memory access pattern.\n\nNow I'm considering whether that requires transposing the input A on upload, but since A = BB^T is numerically symmetric, and the algorithm only ever reads/writes the lower triangle, I can work with a column-major layout without worrying about mismatched upper/lower entries.\n\nDefining the transpose kernels...\n\nStill writing kernel tiling logic...\n\nMultiplication is commutative so the order is exact either way. Checking load balance across columns—work scales like (n-j)*j, so early columns have fewer rows to process while parallelism per launch shrinks as j grows, which could matter for smaller n.\n\nFor larger n like 4096, each launch has up to 4096 threads, which only gives modest GPU occupancy compared to what something like an A100 can handle. I'm considering splitting the k-range across blocks with a 2D grid, but that would require atomics and change the summation order, so to preserve bit-exact results I'd need to keep the sequential accumulation order intact, meaning the GPU stays underutilized for large n since each column launch is capped at n threads.\n\nThe dependency structure is inherently sequential too: column j needs column j-1 finished, and each element's sum is itself a chain of length up to j, so the overall critical path scales roughly like n steps of length n, making true parallel depth closer to O(n²) regardless of how many processors are thrown at it.\n\nI'm deciding to preserve the exact same arithmetic order for bit-identical, hash-reproducible output rather than chase more aggressive parallelism, since the task mentions equivalent semantics but doesn't demand bitwise matching at all costs. I'll consider whether to redundantly recompute the diagonal dot product in every block to avoid a separate kernel launch, but won't over-engineer this further.\n\nI'm estimating the diagonal sum computation cost both as naive global-memory reads and as a shared-memory cooperative reduction, concluding the naive approach is too slow (~0.5ms per column, ~0.1s total) compared to keeping it as a separate kernel launch. i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j <= i; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            \n            if (i == j) {\n                // Diagonal element\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum += A[j * n + k] * A[j * n + k];\n                }\n                const double val = A[j * n + j] - sum;\n                if (val <= 0.0) {\n                    // Matrix is not positive definite\n                    printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", j);\n                    return false;\n                }\n                A[j * n + j] = sqrt(val);\n            } else {\n                // Off-diagonal element\n                for (size_t k = 0; For each column j:\n//   1. diagKernel computes L(j,j) = sqrt(A(j,j) - sum_{k<j} L(j,k)^2)  (single block)\n//   2. colKernel computes L(i,j) = (A(i,j) - sum_{k<j} L(i,k) L(j,k)) / L(j,j)\n//      for all rows i > j in parallel (one thread per row).\n// Every element's dot product is accumulated in the same k = 0..j-1 order as the\n// original sequential code, so the numerical results are the same.\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                          \\\n    do {                                                                          \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s (%s)\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_), #call);                             \\\n            exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                                   \\\n        }                                                                         \\\n    } while (0)\n\nnamespace {\n\nconstexpr int kBlock = 256;        // threads per block for the column/diagonal kernels\nconstexpr int kTile = 32;          // transpose tile edge\nconstexpr size_t kCheckInterval = 128;  // columns between host checks of the failure flag\n\n// dst[c * rows + r] = src[r * cols + c]  (src is rows x cols, dst is cols x rows).\n// If lowerOnly is set, elements with r > c are written as zero (upper triangle).\n__global__ void transposeKernel(const double* __restrict__ src, double* __restrict__ dst,\n                                size_t rows, size_t cols, bool lowerOnly) {\n    __shared__ double tile[kTile][kTile + 1];\n    const size_t c0 = (size_t)blockIdx.x * kTile;\n    const size_t r0 = (size_t)blockIdx.y * kTile;\n\n    for (int dy = threadIdx.y; dy < kTile; dy += blockDim.y) {\n        const size_t r = r0 + dy;\n        const size_t c = c0 + threadIdx.x;\n        if (r < rows && c < cols) {\n            tile[dy][threadIdx.x] = src[r * cols + c];\n        }\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    for (int dy = threadIdx.y; dy < kTile; dy += blockDim.y) {\n        const size_t c = c0 + dy;   // src column == dst row\n        const size_t r = r0 + threadIdx.x;   // src row == dst column\n        if (c < cols && r < rows) {\n            double v = tile[threadIdx.x][dy];\n            if (lowerOnly && r > c) {\n                v = 0.0;\n            }\n            dst[c * rows + r] = v;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Computes the diagonal element L(j,j). Uses a single block; thread 0 performs the\n// sequential accumulation (same order as the reference), with the operands staged\n// through shared memory.\n__global__ void diagKernel(double* __restrict__ W, size_t n, size_t j, int* failCol) {\n    __shared__ double sh[kBlock];\n    double sum = 0.0;\n    for (size_t base = 0; base < j; base += kBlock) {\n        const size_t cnt = (j - base < (size_t)kBlock) ? (j - base) : (size_t)kBlock;\n        if ((size_t)threadIdx.x < cnt) {\n            sh[threadIdx.x] = W[(base + threadIdx.x) * n + j];\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {\n            for (size_t t = 0; t < cnt; ++t) {\n                sum += sh[t] * sh[t];\n            }\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n    if (threadIdx.x == 0) {\n        const double val = W[j * n + j] - sum;\n        if (val <= 0.0) {\n            // Matrix is not positive definite; record the smallest failing index.\n            atomicMin(failCol, (int)j);\n        } else {\n            W[j * n + j] = sqrt(val);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Computes all off-diagonal elements L(i,j) for i > j in parallel.\n__global__ void colKernel(double* __restrict__ W, size_t n, size_t j) {\n    __shared__ double sh[kBlock];\n    const size_t i = j + 1 + (size_t)blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    const bool active = i < n;\n    const double ljj = W[j * n + j];\n\n    double sum = 0.0;\n    for (size_t base = 0; base < j; base += kBlock) {\n        const size_t cnt = (j - base < (size_t)kBlock) ? (j - base) : (size_t)kBlock;\n        if ((size_t)threadIdx.x < cnt) {\n            sh[threadIdx.x] = W[(base + threadIdx.x) * n + j];   // L(j, base + t)\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n        if (active) {\n            for (size_t t = 0; t < cnt; ++t) {\n                sum += W[(base + t) * n + i] * sh[t];           // L(i, k) * L(j, k)\n            }\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n    if (active) {\n        W[j * n + i] = (W[j * n + i] - sum) / ljj;\n    }\n}\n\n}  // namespace\n\n// Initializes the CUDA context so that its one-time cost is not counted in timing.\nvoid initCuda() {\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(nullptr));\n}\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order\n    if (n == 0) {\n        return true;\n    }\n\n    const size_t bytes = n * n * sizeof(double);\n    double* dA = nullptr;   // row-major input / final output\n    double* dW = nullptr;   // column-major working copy\n    int* dFail = nullptr;   // smallest failing diagonal index (INT_MAX if none)\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dA, bytes));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dW, bytes));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dFail, sizeof(int)));\n\n    const int noFail = INT_MAX;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dA, A.data(), bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dFail, &noFail, sizeof(int), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n\n    const dim3 tBlock(kTile, 8);\n    const dim3 tGrid((unsigned)((n + kTile - 1) / kTile), (unsigned)((n + kTile - 1) / kTile));\n\n    // dW[c * n + r] = A(r, c)\n    transposeKernel<<<tGrid, tBlock>>>(dA, dW, n, n, false);\n\n    int failCol = noFail;\n    for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n        diagKernel<<<1, kBlock>>>(dW, n, j, dFail);\n        const size_t rows = n - j - 1;\n        if (rows > 0) {\n            const unsigned blocks = (unsigned)((rows + kBlock - 1) / kBlock);\n            colKernel<<<blocks, kBlock>>>(dW, n, j);\n        }\n        if ((j + 1) % kCheckInterval == 0 || j + 1 == n) {\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(&failCol, dFail, sizeof(int), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n            if (failCol != noFail) {\n                break;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n\n    if (failCol != noFail) {\n        printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %d\\n\", failCol);\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dA));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dW));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dFail));\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // dA[i * n + j] = L(i, j) for j <= i, zero otherwise\n    transposeKernel<<<tGrid, tBlock>>>(dW, dA, n, n, true);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(A.data(), dA, bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n\n I should try printing out the full matrix at n=6 to find exactly which element diverges first, rather than relying on the summary output.\n\nActually I think I found it: nvcc compiles host code with `-std=c++20` in strict ISO mode rather than GNU mode, and GCC defaults to `-ffp-contract=off` in ISO mode — unlike the original CMake build which likely uses gnu++20 and gets FMA contraction by default. That would explain why the GPU build's CPU-side matrix generation differs numerically. I want to verify by rebuilding the original with `-std=c++20 -O3 -march=native` and checking if its hashes now match the CUDA build's at n=6.\n\n","time":{"start":1792984324466,"end":1792984331550},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

I'm now looking at the CUDA flags, specifically the generate-code arch spec targeting compute_52/sm_52.\n\nCMake's \"native\" architecture detection apparently failed and fell back to compute_52 instead of the 3090's actual sm_86, which means the code runs via PTX JIT compilation rather than native sm_86 code. While JIT should theoretically preserve identical arithmetic, I shouldn't rely on broken native detection anyway — I should set an explicit architecture list covering CUDA 12.0's supported targets, something like 70;75;80;86;89;90 to include Hopper.\n\nNow I want to rebuild with that explicit list and see if the hash mismatch changes, then trace the first diverging element to confirm whether the fp-contract/ptxas hypothesis holds.\n\n","time":{"start":1792984346617,"end":1792984352633},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1792984495802,"sessionID":"ses_e89d38de8ffeZMnUEMUMxm8TOL","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01YNqPeYR1w34v5uPAGmpFk8","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r2/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","content":"#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <climits>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// CUDA Cholesky decomposition (left-looking, column-oriented).\n// Decomposes positive definite matrix A into L * L^T where L is lower triangular.\n//\n// The factorization runs on the GPU. The working copy W is column-major:\n// W[c * n + r] holds element (r, c), so the entries of one column are contiguous\n// across rows and warp accesses are coalesced.\n//\n// For each column j (one kernel launch per column):\n//   - L(j,j) = sqrt(A(j,j) - sum_{k<j} L(j,k)^2). The running sum of squares\n//     dacc[j] already holds sum_{k<j} L(j,k)^2, accumulated in k order, so every\n//     block evaluates this in O(1).\n//   - For all rows i > j in parallel:\n//       L(i,j) = (A(i,j) - sum_{k<j} L(i,k) * L(j,k)) / L(j,j)\n//     and dacc[i] += L(i,j)^2.\n// Each dot product is accumulated in the same k = 0..j-1 order as the original\n// sequential code. The diagonal is written back once all columns are processed.\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                          \\\n    do {                                                                          \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s (%s)\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_), #call);                             \\\n            exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                                   \\\n        }                                                                         \\\n    } while (0)\n\nnamespace {\n\nconstexpr int kBlock = 256;             // threads per block for the column kernel\nconstexpr int kTile = 32;               // transpose tile edge\nconstexpr size_t kCheckInterval = 128;  // columns between host checks of the failure flag\n\n// dst[c * rows + r] = src[r * cols + c]  (src is rows x cols, dst is cols x rows).\n// If lowerOnly is set, elements with r > c are written as zero (upper triangle).\n__global__ void transposeKernel(const double* __restrict__ src, double* __restrict__ dst,\n                                size_t rows, size_t cols, bool lowerOnly) {\n    __shared__ double tile[kTile][kTile + 1];\n    const size_t c0 = (size_t)blockIdx.x * kTile;\n    const size_t r0 = (size_t)blockIdx.y * kTile;\n\n    for (int dy = threadIdx.y; dy < kTile; dy += blockDim.y) {\n        const size_t r = r0 + dy;\n        const size_t c = c0 + threadIdx.x;\n        if (r < rows && c < cols) {\n            tile[dy][threadIdx.x] = src[r * cols + c];\n        }\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    for (int dy = threadIdx.y; dy < kTile; dy += blockDim.y) {\n        const size_t c = c0 + dy;            // src column == dst row\n        const size_t r = r0 + threadIdx.x;   // src row == dst column\n        if (c < cols && r < rows) {\n            double v = tile[threadIdx.x][dy];\n            if (lowerOnly && r > c) {\n                v = 0.0;\n            }\n            dst[c * rows + r] = v;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Processes column j: computes L(j,j) (redundantly in every block) and all\n// L(i,j) for i > j in parallel.\n__global__ void columnKernel(double* __restrict__ W, double* __restrict__ dacc, size_t n,\n                             size_t j, int* failCol) {\n    __shared__ double sh[kBlock];\n\n    // L(j,j) = sqrt(A(j,j) - sum_{k<j} L(j,k)^2). Diagonal of W still holds A(j,j).\n    const double diagVal = W[j * n + j] - dacc[j];\n    if (diagVal <= 0.0) {\n        // Matrix is not positive definite; record the smallest failing index.\n        if (blockIdx.x == 0 && threadIdx.x == 0) {\n            atomicMin(failCol, (int)j);\n        }\n    }\n    const double ljj = sqrt(diagVal);\n\n    const size_t i = j + 1 + (size_t)blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    const bool active = i < n;\n\n    double sum = 0.0;\n    for (size_t base = 0; base < j; base += kBlock) {\n        const size_t cnt = (j - base < (size_t)kBlock) ? (j - base) : (size_t)kBlock;\n        if ((size_t)threadIdx.x < cnt) {\n            sh[threadIdx.x] = W[(base + threadIdx.x) * n + j];  // L(j, base + t)\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n        if (active) {\n            for (size_t t = 0; t < cnt; ++t) {\n                sum += W[(base + t) * n + i] * sh[t];           // L(i,k) * L(j,k)\n            }\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n    if (active) {\n        const double lij = (W[j * n + i] - sum) / ljj;\n        W[j * n + i] = lij;\n        dacc[i] += lij * lij;\n    }\n}\n\n// Writes the final diagonal L(j,j) = sqrt(A(j,j) - dacc[j]) into W.\n__global__ void finalizeDiagonalKernel(double* __restrict__ W, const double* __restrict__ dacc,\n                                       size_t n) {\n    const size_t j = (size_t)blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (j < n) {\n        W[j * n + j] = sqrt(W[j * n + j] - dacc[j]);\n    }\n}\n\n}  // namespace\n\n// Initializes the CUDA context so that its one-time cost is not counted in timing.\nvoid initCuda() {\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(nullptr));\n}\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order\n    if (n == 0) {\n        return true;\n    }\n\n    const size_t bytes = n * n * sizeof(double);\n    const size_t vecBytes = n * sizeof(double);\n    double* dA = nullptr;     // row-major input / final output\n    double* dW = nullptr;     // column-major working copy\n    double* dAcc = nullptr;   // dAcc[i] = sum_{k<j} L(i,k)^2 at the start of column j\n    int* dFail = nullptr;     // smallest failing diagonal index (INT_MAX if none)\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dA, bytes));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dW, bytes));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dAcc, vecBytes));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dFail, sizeof(int)));\n\n    const int noFail = INT_MAX;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dA, A.data(), bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dFail, &noFail, sizeof(int), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemset(dAcc, 0, vecBytes));\n\n    const dim3 tBlock(kTile, 8);\n    const unsigned tiles = (unsigned)((n + kTile - 1) / kTile);\n    const dim3 tGrid(tiles, tiles);\n\n    // dW[c * n + r] = A(r, c)\n    transposeKernel<<<tGrid, tBlock>>>(dA, dW, n, n, false);\n\n    int failCol = noFail;\n    for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n        const size_t rows = n - j - 1;\n        // At least one block is launched so that the diagonal check always runs.\n        const unsigned blocks = (rows > 0) ? (unsigned)((rows + kBlock - 1) / kBlock) : 1u;\n        columnKernel<<<blocks, kBlock>>>(dW, dAcc, n, j, dFail);\n        if ((j + 1) % kCheckInterval == 0 || j + 1 == n) {\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(&failCol, dFail, sizeof(int), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n            if (failCol != noFail) {\n                break;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n\n    if (failCol != noFail) {\n        printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %d\\n\", failCol);\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dA));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dW));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dAcc));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dFail));\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    finalizeDiagonalKernel<<<(unsigned)((n + kBlock - 1) / kBlock), kBlock>>>(dW, dAcc, n);\n\n    // dA[i * n + j] = L(i, j) for j <= i, zero otherwise\n    transposeKernel<<<tGrid, tBlock>>>(dW, dA, n, n, true);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(A.data(), dA, bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dA));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dW));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dAcc));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dFail));\n    return true;\n}\n\n// Generate a symmetric positive definite matrix\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // Method: Create A = B * B^T where B is random\n    // This guarantees A is positive semi-definite\n    // Then add identity to make it strictly positive definite\n\n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n\n    // Generate random matrix B\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        B[i] = (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 0.5;\n    }\n\n    // Compute A = B * B^T\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += B[i * n + k] * B[j * n + k];\n            }\n            A[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Add diagonal dominance to ensure positive definiteness\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i * n + i] += n;\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateCholesky(const std::vector<double>& L, const std::vector<double>& A_orig, const size_t n) {\n    // Validate by computing L * L^T and comparing with original matrix\n\n    std::vector<double> reconstructed(n * n);\n\n    // Compute L * L^T\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += L[i * n + k] * L[j * n + k];\n            }\n            reconstructed[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Compare with original\n    double maxError = 0.0;\n    double relError = 0.0;\n\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        const double error = fabs(reconstructed[i] - A_orig[i]);\n        maxError = std::max(maxError, error);\n\n        const double rel = error / (fabs(A_orig[i]) + 1e-10);\n        relError = std::max(relError, rel);\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Max absolute error: %.10e\\n\", maxError);\n    printf(\"Max relative error: %.10e\\n\", relError);\n\n    // Check if error is within tolerance\n    if (relError > 1e-6) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: relative error too large\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t n = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            n = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Cholesky Decomposition Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", n, n);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n\n    // Allocate matrix\n    std::vector<double> A(n * n);\n    std::vector<double> A_orig;\n\n    // Generate positive definite matrix\n    printf(\"Generating positive definite matrix...\\n\");\n    generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(A, n);\n\n    if (validate) {\n        A_orig = A; // Save original for validation\n    }\n\n    // Perform Cholesky decomposition\n    printf(\"Computing Cholesky decomposition...\\n\");\n    initCuda();  // exclude one-time CUDA context creation from the timing\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    bool success = choleskyDecomposition(A, n);\n\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n\n    if (!success) {\n        printf(\"Cholesky decomposition failed\\n\");\n        return 1;\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n\n    // Calculate GFLOPS (approximately n³/3 operations for Cholesky)\n    double ops = (double)n * n * n / 3.0;\n    double gflops = ops / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n    printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n\n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults) {\n        print_results(A, \"CholeskyL\");\n    }\n\n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n        bool valid = validateCholesky(A, A_orig, n);\n\n        if (valid) {\n            printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    return 0;\n}\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r2/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","exists":true,"truncated":false},"title":"home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r2/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","time":{"start":1792984495729,"end":1792984495768}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_17633fc270016aXsIU2IneoKP2","sessionID":"ses_e89d38de8ffeZMnUEMUMxm8TOL","messageID":"msg_17633f214001rjx9cfgMggY8Gx"}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1792984941222,"sessionID":"ses_e89d38de8ffeZMnUEMUMxm8TOL","part":{"id":"prt_1763aa8500014T3PqbrnVBfppD","messageID":"msg_1763aa3ea0010ubStYEzuN8IR7","sessionID":"ses_e89d38de8ffeZMnUEMUMxm8TOL","type":"reasoning","text":"Unrolling by 4 gives 180ms, barely faster than unrolling by 8's 197ms, so the real constraint is parallelism, not loop structure. With only ~1024 active threads averaged across 82 SMs, occupancy is extremely low, and each thread runs a dependent chain of roughly j FMAs, which is clearly the bottleneck.\n\nI consider splitting each row's dot product across multiple threads, but since the second half depends sequentially on the first, that breaks exact-order summation. Preserving exact summation order means accepting a cost scaling with n² times latency — relaxing to tree or blocked sums would change rounding behavior, so I'll stick with the exact-order approach and settle on unroll factor 4 as the best tradeoff.\n\nNow I'm thinking about \"parallel scalability\" more carefully — a row-per-thread design only gives n threads per launch, which scales poorly on larger GPUs. I'm exploring whether a row-wavefront design, where each block computes a row sequentially while depending on previously finished rows, could preserve exact ordering while improving scalability.\n\nI'm worried about whether all row-blocks can stay co-resident on the GPU for large n, since spin-wait synchronization requires earlier rows to actually be scheduled before later ones depend on them. But since blocks are dispatched in increasing index order, earlier rows always launch first, so even without full co-residency the dependency order is naturally respected and deadlock shouldn't occur.\n\nIf I assign one thread per row to do the sequential accumulation, most of each warp sits idle, and the real bottleneck becomes the latency chain — with roughly n²/2 dependent memory loads and FMAs, each paying full DRAM/L2 latency, the total time scales brutally for n=2048.\n\nThe column-wise approach actually has the same critical path length (n²/2 sequential steps), so row-wavefront ordering doesn't help unless the per-thread chain itself gets shorter. My measured ~90ns per dependent step roughly matches global-memory latency, which tells me I'm fundamentally latency-bound along this dependency chain — the only way to beat it is to get the dependent data into shared memory to cut per-step latency way down.\n\nActually wait — column j needs k from 0 to j-1, so column j+1 needs all the same k values plus one more. That means consecutive columns share nearly all their k-data, so caching the tile in shared memory and incrementally extending it as j grows could give substantial reuse.\n\nGiven this, I'm weighing whether full row-block caching fits in shared memory versus L2 — it doesn't fit in smem but might partially fit in L2 depending on GPU size, so I'm leaning toward accepting the current ~180ms result at n=2048 as a solid 12x speedup rather than chasing marginal caching gains.\n\nLooking closer at the coalescing pattern, each warp's load for a fixed k is already contiguous and efficient, but the achieved bandwidth (~64 GB/s) is far below peak, meaning the kernel is latency-bound rather than bandwidth-bound — so deeper prefetching/unrolling is the likely next lever, though gains so far have been modest.\n\nWith only about 12 threads active per SM, occupancy is already far too low for the extra parallelism to matter — the row count limits how many threads can actually be used.\n\nSince maintaining exact order with column kernels forces a latency-bound ~n²/2 sequential path, I'll accept that constraint and settle on kUnroll=4, since block size doesn't affect latency here. I'll update the file with this value, rebuild, and verify hashes and validation at moderate sizes, then check the non-PD test case and confirm flags like -h still work, possibly running a quick sanitizer pass at n=100 to catch memory issues.\n\n","time":{"start":1792984918096,"end":1792984941118},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
